q: The Zero flag in the processor status register is set when
options: A carry is generated out of the most significant bit
The result of the last ALU operation is zero
The result of the last operation is negative
exp: The Z flag records that the ALU result was all zeros; carry, sign and overflow have their own flags.

q: A 16-bit instruction uses 4-bit address fields and an expanding opcode. There are 14 three-address instructions and 30 two-address instructions. What is the maximum number of one-address instructions possible?
exp: 3-address: 2 of 16 opcodes remain; each gives 16 two-address codes = 32, of which 30 are used, leaving 2; each of those gives 16 one-address codes = 32.

q: Main memory is 16 MB, the cache is 64 KB, the block size is 32 bytes and the cache is 4-way set associative. The number of tag bits is
exp: Address = 24 bits; offset = 5; lines = 2¹⁶/2⁵ = 2¹¹; sets = 2¹¹/4 = 2⁹; tag = 24 - 5 - 9 = 10 bits.

q:
Assertion (A): RISC processors generally achieve higher pipeline efficiency than CISC processors.
Reason (R): RISC instructions are simple, of fixed length and take a uniform time to execute.
options: Both A and R are false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
exp: Uniform, simple fixed-length instructions make pipeline stages balanced and easy to decode, so the pipeline stalls less.

q: In daisy-chain bus arbitration, the priority of a device is decided by
options: The device number stored in a register
Its position along the chain relative to the arbiter
exp: The grant signal passes through devices in series, so the device nearest the arbiter has the highest priority.

q: Which type of read-only memory can be erased by exposure to ultraviolet light and then reprogrammed?
exp: EPROM has a quartz window for UV erasure; EEPROM is erased electrically.

An instruction ADD R1, @500 uses memory indirect addressing: location 500 holds 800 and location 800 holds the operand. Assuming the instruction occupies one word, how many memory accesses are needed to fetch and complete the operand read?
exp: One access for the instruction, one to read the pointer at 500 and one to read the operand at 800: 3 accesses.

q: Which type of cache miss is completely eliminated by making the cache fully associative (with the same size)?
exp: Conflict misses occur when blocks compete for the same set; a fully associative cache has no such restriction.

q: Which statement best describes a superscalar processor?
options: It can issue more than one instruction per clock cycle using multiple execution units
A single instruction operates on whole vectors of data
It executes exactly one instruction at a time
It shares one execution unit among many threads by time slicing only
exp: Superscalar designs dispatch several instructions per cycle to parallel functional units.

q: A division by zero during program execution causes an interrupt which is classified as
exp: Interrupts caused by the executing program itself, such as divide-by-zero or overflow, are internal interrupts (traps).

q: A program has 25% serial code. The maximum speedup possible with an unlimited number of processors, according to Amdahl's law, is
exp: Maximum speedup = 1 / serial fraction = 1 / 0.25 = 4.

q: A processor runs at 2 GHz with an average CPI of 2 and executes 10⁹ instructions. The execution time is
exp: Time = (10⁹ × 2) / (2 × 10⁹) = 1 second.

q:
Match each instruction with its category:
1. MOV   2. ADD   3. JMP   4. IN
P. Arithmetic   Q. Data transfer   R. Control transfer   S. Input/output
exp: MOV moves data, ADD is arithmetic, JMP changes control flow and IN reads from an I/O port.

q: In a 4-way low-order interleaved memory, the address 26 is located in which bank?
exp: Bank number = address mod 4 = 26 mod 4 = 2.

q: Thrashing in a virtual memory system refers to
options: The cache being overwritten too often
Excessive paging activity so that the system spends more time swapping pages than executing
exp: Thrashing occurs when processes lack enough frames, causing continuous page faults and little useful work.

q: A pipeline has a clock period of 2 ns. In the steady state (ignoring start-up), the number of instructions completed per second is
exp: One instruction completes per cycle: 1 / 2 ns = 5 × 10⁸ per second.

q: Which of the following interfaces transfers data serially, one bit at a time, over a pair of data lines?
exp: USB is a serial bus, whereas the others listed are parallel interfaces.

q:
Statement I: A solid-state drive has no mechanical moving parts.
Statement II: The access time of a hard disk includes seek time and rotational latency.
Which is correct?
exp: SSDs are built from flash chips, while a hard disk must move the head to the track and wait for the sector to rotate under it.

q:
Match each generation with its key technology:
1. First   2. Second   3. Third   4. Fourth
P. Transistors   Q. VLSI microprocessors   R. Vacuum tubes   S. Integrated circuits
exp: Vacuum tubes (1st), transistors (2nd), ICs (3rd), VLSI microprocessors (4th).

q: The main advantage of a carry look-ahead adder over a ripple-carry adder is that it
options: Eliminates the need for sum bits
Reduces carry propagation delay by computing carries in parallel
exp: Look-ahead logic generates all carries from generate/propagate signals instead of waiting for each stage.

q: A stack machine executes: PUSH 4, PUSH 6, PUSH 2, SUB, MUL, PUSH 5, ADD. SUB computes (second from top) - (top) and MUL, ADD act on the top two items. The final value on the stack is
exp: Stack: 4,6,2 → SUB gives 6-2=4 → 4,4 → MUL gives 16 → PUSH 5 → ADD gives 21.

q: In a write-back cache, the dirty bit of a line indicates that
options: The block was modified after being loaded and must be written to memory before being replaced
The block is locked in the cache
The block has never been accessed
exp: Write-back defers memory updates; the dirty bit marks lines needing a write-back on eviction.

q: A RISC program executes 1.3 × 10⁹ instructions with CPI 1.2; the equivalent CISC program executes 10⁹ instructions with CPI 3. Both run at the same clock rate. How many times faster is the RISC version?
exp: Cycles: RISC = 1.56 × 10⁹, CISC = 3 × 10⁹; speedup = 3 / 1.56 ≈ 1.92.

q: In asynchronous data transfer using handshaking, the two units coordinate using
options: A common clock shared by both
Control signals indicating that data is valid and that data has been accepted
exp: Handshaking uses request/acknowledge (data valid / data accepted) signals instead of a shared clock.

q: Pipelining a processor is mainly an example of which kind of parallelism?
exp: Overlapping the execution of different stages of successive instructions is instruction-level parallelism.

q: A stack grows toward lower addresses and the stack pointer initially holds 5000. After three PUSH operations of 2-byte values, the stack pointer holds
exp: Each push decrements SP by 2: 5000 - 3 × 2 = 4994.

q: A branch instruction located at address 2000 uses PC-relative addressing. The PC has already been incremented by 4 and the offset is -12. The branch target address is
exp: Target = PC + offset = 2004 - 12 = 1992.

q: A direct-mapped cache has 8 lines. Block addresses 2, 10, 2, 3, 2, 3 are referenced in order (cache initially empty). The number of hits is
exp: Blocks 2 and 10 both map to line 2: misses on 2, 10, 2, and a miss on 3; then 2 and 3 hit, giving 2 hits.

q: In a 5-stage pipeline with full forwarding, a load instruction is immediately followed by an instruction that uses the loaded value. How many stall cycles are required?
exp: The loaded data is available only after MEM, so even with forwarding one bubble is needed (load-use hazard).

q: A program has 40% ALU instructions (CPI 1), 30% load/store instructions (CPI 2) and 30% branches (CPI 3). The average CPI is
The auto-increment addressing mode is especially useful for
exp: The register used as pointer is incremented automatically after each access, stepping through consecutive elements.

q: A direct-mapped cache of 16 KB uses 64-byte blocks and 32-bit addresses. The total number of tag bits stored in the cache (ignoring valid and dirty bits) is
exp: Lines = 256 (8 index bits), offset = 6 bits, tag = 32 - 8 - 6 = 18 bits; 18 × 256 = 4608 bits.

q: Compared with a 1-bit branch predictor, a 2-bit saturating counter predictor mainly avoids
options: Two mispredictions per execution of a loop (at exit and at re-entry)
exp: A single anomalous outcome (loop exit) does not flip a 2-bit prediction, so a repeated loop is mispredicted only once.

q: Why does the CPU save the program counter and status word when an interrupt is accepted?
options: To make the interrupt service routine run faster
To resume the interrupted program correctly after the service routine finishes
exp: The saved context is restored on return from the ISR so the interrupted program continues as if nothing happened.

q: In a shared-memory multiprocessor, the cache coherence problem arises because
options: Several private caches may hold different copies of the same memory location
exp: When one processor updates its cached copy, other caches may hold stale values unless a coherence protocol is used.

q: A hard disk rotates at 7200 RPM. Its average rotational latency is approximately
exp: One rotation takes 60/7200 = 8.33 ms; average latency is half of that, 4.17 ms.

q: A system bus is 32 bits wide, runs at 100 MHz and transfers one word per clock cycle. Its maximum data transfer rate is
exp: 4 bytes × 100 × 10⁶ transfers per second = 400 MB/s.

q: Memory access time is 100 ns and the page-fault service time is 8 ms. If the page-fault rate is 1 in 10⁵ accesses, the effective access time is approximately
The number of bits that a CPU can process as a single unit in one operation is called its
exp: Word length is the natural unit of data (e.g. 32 or 64 bits) the processor handles at once.
